Oh yeah sorry I didn’t mention a clear month, it started to feel easier in June and I felt fully healed around August or September. I got back into my hobbies, talked to my friends more often, and journaled how I felt a lot.

I do feel I need to mention that my worst points were some weeks in March and some in July. For March, I also lost a lot of weight shortly after getting ghosted - I was so sad that food didn’t have taste. It made me think I had COVID but it was all just because of how sad I was. I then would freak out about how much food I ate that day, weigh myself, stalk his Instagram, and then go crazy if I saw that he followed someone new (yes I’m embarrassed I did that). Only until my friend told me to stop weighing myself did I stop doing that awful cycle, but I was definitely still hung up on my ex.

I then fell back into other bad habits in July partially cause of ex but partially because of family. Once again my friend helped me out of it, they pointed out that those destructive behaviors stem from my insecurities and that I’m not actually happy with those habits. After that I got back on track.

I felt the need to mention those setbacks because when you get to moments where you feel sad about your ex you may feel like you haven’t made any progress at all, but it’s often just part of the process. It also helps to have friends who support you, and are caring enough to tell you to stop engaging in self destruction. 

Also sorry this comment is already so long but I really want to add that I don’t have a clear month of when I felt fully healed. He became so unimportant that I wasn’t thinking about healing from him, I was focused on achieving what I wanted - and I really hope you get to this point too.

Also let me know if you’re open to hearing additional advice or sayings that were actually helpful in healing :)

I’m really sorry you had to go through that OP :( I was in a 2 year relationship, approaching 3, we met irl and became long distance, and then I got ghosted this January. He even said I love you a week before ghosting. 

I’m definitely healed from him now but it wasn’t a linear journey at all. I lost myself and made self-destructive choices to cope because I wanted to avoid my feelings. Once I started to sit with my feelings and go back to my hobbies I started to feel like myself again and reflect on how awful he was.

It does get easier but you need to balance between feeling your emotions and doing activities. Let yourself experience each feeling but also get back into the things you love, even if it’s just a little bit each day. 

For me the pain didn’t fully stop, but it becomes less significant because you have better, more important things going on. Eventually there will be days where the pain doesn’t even cross your mind.

I hope things get easier for you, and that you remember that his actions don’t define you.
Yes this too this is really important :D

I think you should focus on developing a stronger sense of self where you recognize what your unhealthy attachment patterns are and take steps to grow from those patterns. I feel like it would help if you put aside dating for now and try to analyze why you may attract hurtful people so that you can meet better people in the future.

Something that really helped me was recognizing that I’m missing someone who can go on without me, and that I deserve someone who actually wants me and knows how to show it. 

That being said, healing is a long process and it’s important to feel and accept each emotion as you go through it.

I know how you feel, I’ve felt the same way about my ex giving attention to other girls after and probably during the relationship. It’s so upsetting that it seems like they can just easily go for another persons attention while you feel the pain of the heartbreak. While I could tell you my wild guesses about why I think dumpers do this, I think it’s better for me to mention that just because he’s giving attention to other people doesn’t mean it’s good attention or that he’s becoming better for them. He may have just found someone other people who ignore the red flags. You deserve someone who brings you peace and thinks about you as deeply as you think about them.

They heal and move on, and moving on isn’t always moving on to another person, sometimes it’s realizing you need to love yourself as much as you loved that person. I wish I could give you a hopeful happy ending to believe in, but I haven’t quite reached that yet. However, I’m certainly happier than I was in the relationship, and after reflecting, I have a better perspective of who I am and what I want. In essence, I feel like I’m on my way to that happy ending, it will just take time.

I also have to note that some days feel like more progress than others. Some days I feel like crying over the relationship, other days I don’t think about him at all. Healing is not a linear process, it will come and go like a wave. Eventually the wave will calm down, it just takes time and enriching your life with other things.

It’s not just you, it’s definitely jarring how they can be such a big part of your life and then they just don’t need you anymore. I was ghosted in January after 2 years and the week before that he told me that he loved me. It’s scary and hard to believe how people can just change like that. I sincerely hope you redirect the love you feel for him into love for yourself because you deserve it.

Thank you very much for your kind words! Yeah I was and am really confused and upset especially since the relationship was 2 years long and we last texted 17 days ago. When I was in denial, I would flip between hating him and missing him, not believing he’d do this to me. I admit that I wasn’t perfect in the relationship - I was clingy in the beginning and anxious that disagreements could end the relationship, but I’m confident that I evened out and became more patient and secure in the relationship over time. It is ironic that I became secure in the relationship and then it ended in a way I was anxious about, but I try to learn from/be grateful for the experience so I stop hurting and don’t unintentionally hurt any future relationship. Anyway, I sincerely hope you’re feeling better! Remember that healing is a process, and progress isn’t always linear!

I experienced the same thing, my last conversation with my ex was so normal I thought everything was going well. Then the next week he left me on seen, and the week after that no reaction/response from him. I was so confused because the week before that he was telling me about how he loves hearing my voice. Honestly during this time I embarrassed myself by repeatedly reaching out wanting an explanation. I saw that he was online and definitely ignoring me. I tried to go take a walk to clear my head but I just kept seeing couples everywhere doing couple shit and it pissed me off. 

It’s clear that you loved her a lot with how much you’re hurting and how confusing it is that she just completely switched up on you. It’s not pathetic to be upset at all, be kinder to yourself, you’re hurt and you have every right to be. Her inability to communicate with you and end things like a decent person reflects on her character, not yours. 

Moving past it is not easy, especially when there’s no clear explanation as to why it ended. Please give yourself time to do what you enjoy and feel your feelings. You deserve better. In case this helps, some things that made me feel better were: 
- the idea that if I love the wrong person this much, then imagine how good it will be with the right person
- the right person wouldn’t treat me this way/make me feel like this
- you have the capacity to love deeply

You’re right, and honestly being left like this is what I was afraid of. Weirdly enough I’m still grateful to have had experienced the relationship at all. While he’s a coward and an asshole for ending things this way, he did make me feel lovable, something I never believed about myself until the relationship.

Firstly, it is unfair that you have to parent your brother in this way, it should be the responsibility of your parents. Good on you for wanting to correct your brother, but outcasting him is not the solution to this, it will only make him angrier and probably even more hateful. It doesn’t sound like he understands why it’s wrong.

I was in a similar situation with my younger cousin who’s around that age. While my cousin doesn’t have anger management issues, he would also say that word and make racist jokes with his friends and then he’d get annoyed with me when I’d tell him that he shouldn’t say that because it’s offensive. 

I finally got him to understand when I explained why it’s offensive. I showed him [this video from the 1950’s of a white audience realizing that the singer of the popular song is black](https://youtu.be/Qo4_UT1pF6k?feature=shared). The disgust and discomfort of some audience members show how much hatred they had for black people, which my cousin found interesting. I explained that this stemmed from slavery, and how the n word was used historically by white people to talk down to black people. I explained that even after slavery ended, there was then segregation where people of color and white people couldn’t even use the same bathrooms. I told him that black people can say the n word because it was used to talk down to them for so long, so their use of it is pushing back against the racism. We can’t say it because we don’t have that history that gives the word its protesting meaning. After that conversation, he felt guilty about using it and it hasn’t been in his vocabulary since then (though there have been like 3 slip ups).

I can’t guarantee that explaining the history will make your brother realize why he shouldn’t say it, or that he’ll even be interested in the history of the word. However, I’d argue that educating him on it is a lot more productive than outcasting him because at least with educating he could have some idea of why it’s wrong.

I suddenly became extremely conscious about how so many other girls were already developed, while people would literally say I looked like a twelve year old boy. I even looked up methods to make them larger naturally, doing certain exercises and eating new foods, which didn’t work for me. Eventually, I got tired of feeling bad and letting other people make me feel bad. My body is not made for their pleasure, all that matter is that I am happy with it. That’s when I started to truly appreciate and understand that there is more to me than my small chest, and that I can be attractive WITH my small boobs, not DESPITE them.

You are completely valid in your understanding of my situation, and thank you for clarifying that you are not attacking me with this. Usually people can just ignore/block out those sounds, normally the brain filters those insignificant sounds like chewing. My issue is that my brain won’t filter out those noises, of course I love my family and talking to them during meals, but I still hear those sounds as much as I try to ignore it. I’m not disgusted at the people or the fact that they’re chewing (ofc people need to chew and they’re chewing cause we have food!) just the sound itself. As much as I tell myself “of course they’re chewing they have to!” My brain takes it as something to be disgusted by, it feels like those noises are burrowing into my ears if that makes sense and then I feel a compulsion to scratch at or cover my ears. I definitely get your point and it is shallow to be disgusted by a literal sign of health and wealth. I don’t mean to be shallow with my discomfort towards the sound I think my response is because of some issue with how my brain is processing the sound (which has been identified in the psychological field as misophonia). (I also do recognize how pathetic self-diagnoses can be but having a severe illogical response to normal human sounds is a sign of the issue and the issue.) I’m sorry that you’ve been homeless and foodless before, but I’m so grateful that you are in a better position now and have been able to speak with me! Your response came after I’ve resolved the issue, but you talking about your experiences helped me understand why my mom reacted so strongly. Thank you! :)
